examples: Why is a foot called a foot?
Why are horses measured in hands?

explain.say: Imagine you need to measure a table, but there are no rulers anywhere. What would you use? Your arms and hands, of course! Look at the longest bar. That's a cubit, from your elbow to your fingertip, about 45 centimetres. Ancient Egyptians built pyramids using cubits.

explain.say: Now look at the foot bar, about 30 centimetres. Romans, Greeks and many others measured in feet. And the inch, the tiny bar, began as the width of a thumb. Try it: is your thumb about two and a half centimetres wide?

explain.say: See the horse? People still measure horses in hands, about 10 centimetres each, the width of a grown-up's palm. A pony might be 14 hands tall at the shoulder. How many hands tall do you think you are?

explain.say: Here's the problem: hands and feet come in all sizes! A tall trader's cubit was longer than a short trader's, so people argued about fair amounts. Kings made official measuring rods; Egypt's royal cubit was about 52 centimetres. Can you see why one fixed size helps everyone?

explain.say: Well done! That's why the metric system came, with a metre fixed for everyone. But body units haven't vanished. Phone screens and bike wheels are still measured in inches, and an inch is now exactly 2.54 centimetres. Can you find something at home measured in inches?

faq.a: A cubit is the length from your elbow to the tip of your middle finger, about 45 centimetres. Ancient Egypt used a royal cubit of about 52 centimetres.

faq.q: Why is a foot called a foot?
faq.a: Because it began as the length of a person's foot. The modern foot is fixed at exactly 30.48 centimetres.

faq.q: Why are horses measured in hands?
faq.a: Horse traders used the width of a hand, now fixed at 4 inches or about 10 centimetres, measured from the ground to the top of the shoulders.

faq.q: Where does the inch come from?
faq.a: The inch began as the width of a thumb. Today one inch is exactly 2.54 centimetres.

faq.q: What was wrong with body units?
faq.a: Bodies are different sizes, so measurements changed from person to person. That made trade unfair, so rulers made standard rods, and later the metric system fixed units for everyone.
asks: Why don't we measure with our hands?

facts: One inch is defined as exactly 2.54 centimetres, and one foot as exactly 30.48 centimetres.
A horse's height is measured in hands, each equal to 4 inches, about 10.2 centimetres.
